```{r packages}
library(LDscnR)
library(data.table)
library(SNPRelate)
```

## Overview

The Stage-1 units in `LDscnR` are built from genotypes alone, so they do not
depend on how the association test is done. Any outlier method that returns
one p-value per marker can therefore be combined with them, for example a
genotype-environment association method such as LFMM, a mixed model other
than EMMAX, or a simple regression. The Simes test then combines the marker
p-values within each unit into one p-value per unit, and the significant units
are assembled into outlier regions as in
`vignette("LDscnR_stage1_outlier_regions")`.

This vignette shows the steps with a small regression written in base R, so
that it runs without extra packages. An example with LFMM2 follows at the end.
The requirements for the p-values are few.

- There is one p-value per marker, in the order of `map$marker` or named by
  marker.
- Markers that could not be tested, for example because they are monomorphic,
  get a p-value of 1 rather than `NA`.
- For the permutation null, the same method is run again on permuted
  phenotypes.

## Stage-1 units

The example is the bundled `stickleback` data set (`?stickleback`). Stage 1 is
run exactly as in the other vignettes and never sees the phenotype.

```{r data}
data("stickleback")
GTs <- stickleback$GTs
map <- copy(stickleback$map)
pheno <- copy(stickleback$pheno)
eco <- as.integer(pheno$ecotype == "Marine")
```

```{r stage1, results = "hide"}
gds_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".gds")
gds <- create_gds_from_geno(GTs, map, gds_path)

set.seed(1)
ld_decay <- compute_LD_decay(gds, keep_el = TRUE, slide = 200, n_win_decay = 20, cores = 2)
stage1 <- ld_complexity_reduction(map = map, LD_decay = ld_decay, r2_rho = 0.5, cores = 2)
```

The size floor follows the marker-density rule, with one required member for
every 250 markers per Mb, rounded and never below two.

```{r size-floor}
span_mb <- map[, (max(Pos) - min(Pos)) / 1e6, by = Chr]$V1
size_floor <- max(2L, as.integer(round(nrow(map) / sum(span_mb) / 250)))
size_floor
```

## Marker p-values from another method

The method used here regresses each marker on the phenotype, with sampling
locality as a covariate to absorb differences between localities. Both the
markers and the phenotype are first adjusted for the covariates through a QR
decomposition, so that all markers are tested in one matrix operation. The
test is the usual t test of the partial correlation.

```{r lm-fn}
lm_pvalues <- function(G, y, covars) {
  X0 <- cbind(1, covars)
  qx <- qr(X0)
  yr <- qr.resid(qx, y)
  Gr <- qr.resid(qx, G)
  r  <- colSums(Gr * yr) / sqrt(colSums(Gr^2) * sum(yr^2))
  df <- nrow(G) - qx$rank - 1
  p  <- 2 * pt(-abs(r * sqrt(df / (1 - r^2))), df)
  p[!is.finite(p)] <- 1     # markers that cannot be tested
  setNames(p, colnames(G))
}

covars <- model.matrix(~ pop_locality, pheno)[, -1, drop = FALSE]
p_marker <- lm_pvalues(GTs, eco, covars)
summary(p_marker)
```

## Simes test and outlier regions

`ld_outlier_test()` with `statistic = "simes"` combines the marker p-values
within each tested unit into one Simes p-value, applies Benjamini-Hochberg
correction across the units and assembles the significant units into outlier
regions.

```{r simes}
out <- ld_outlier_test(stage1, map, p_marker, statistic = "simes",
                       size_floor = size_floor, alpha = 0.05,
                       assembly = "stage2_discovered", GTs = GTs, LD_decay = ld_decay)
out
out$regions
```

```{r manhattan}
region_members <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(out$regions)), function(i) {
  r <- out$regions[i]
  map[Chr == r$Chr & Pos >= r$from & Pos <= r$to, marker]
})
ld_manhattan(map, value = -log10(p_marker), value_label = expression(-log[10](p)),
             regions = region_members, point_size = 1.5)
```

The consensus test works with another method as well. `ld_unit_matrix()`
builds one consensus value per unit and individual, the method tests these
values instead of the markers, and the unit p-values are passed with
`statistic = "unit"`.

```{r consensus}
m_cons <- ld_unit_matrix(GTs, stage1, map, size_floor = size_floor, repr = "consensus_dosage")
p_unit <- lm_pvalues(m_cons, eco, covars)
out_unit <- ld_outlier_test(stage1, map, p_unit, statistic = "unit",
                            size_floor = size_floor, alpha = 0.05,
                            assembly = "stage2_discovered", GTs = GTs, LD_decay = ld_decay)
out_unit$regions
```

## Permutation null with the same method

The permutation null asks how many units the same workflow would call
significant if the phenotype carried no information beyond the structure that
the null preserves. The method is therefore run again on each permuted
phenotype, with the same covariates. Ecotype is shuffled within locality, which
keeps each locality's share of marine and freshwater fish. The permuted
p-values are collected into a matrix with one row per marker and one column per
permutation.

```{r perm}
B <- 40L
set.seed(1)
p_perm <- vapply(seq_len(B), function(b) {
  eco_perm <- ave(eco, pheno$pop_locality, FUN = sample)
  lm_pvalues(GTs, eco_perm, covars)
}, numeric(ncol(GTs)))
dim(p_perm)

null_units <- ld_outlier_perm(out, stage1, map, p_perm, level = "units", verbose = FALSE)
null_units
```

As in the main outlier vignette, `null_obs_ratio` is the mean number of
discoveries under the null divided by the observed number. It is not a false
discovery rate and says nothing about any single region. Forty permutations
are used here only to keep the vignette fast, and a real analysis should use
many more.

## An example with LFMM2

LFMM2 from the `LEA` package tests genotype-environment associations while
correcting for population structure with latent factors. Its calibrated
p-values can be used in the same way. The chunk below is not run when the
vignette is built, so that `LEA` is not required. The number of latent factors
`K` should be chosen for the data set, for example from a PCA screeplot or
from `snmf()` cross-entropy.

```{r lfmm2, eval = FALSE}
library(LEA)

lfmm_pvalues <- function(G, env, K) {
  mod <- lfmm2(input = G, env = env, K = K)
  p <- as.numeric(lfmm2.test(mod, input = G, env = env,
                             genomic.control = TRUE)$pvalues)
  p[!is.finite(p)] <- 1
  setNames(p, colnames(G))
}

p_lfmm <- lfmm_pvalues(GTs, eco, K = 7)
out_lfmm <- ld_outlier_test(stage1, map, p_lfmm, statistic = "simes",
                            size_floor = size_floor, alpha = 0.05,
                            assembly = "stage2_discovered", GTs = GTs, LD_decay = ld_decay)

# permutation null with the same method, here with fewer permutations
# because each LFMM2 fit takes longer
p_perm_lfmm <- vapply(seq_len(B), function(b) {
  lfmm_pvalues(GTs, ave(eco, pheno$pop_locality, FUN = sample), K = 7)
}, numeric(ncol(GTs)))
ld_outlier_perm(out_lfmm, stage1, map, p_perm_lfmm, level = "units")
```

Methods that return a statistic rather than a p-value, such as Bayes factors
or XtX from BayPass, need calibrated p-values first, for example from
simulated pseudo-observed data sets or from the empirical distribution of the
statistic.

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
SNPRelate::snpgdsClose(gds)
unlink(gds_path)
```

## Summary

- Stage-1 units are built from genotypes alone and can be combined with any
  outlier method that gives one p-value per marker.
- The Simes test combines the marker p-values within each unit, and the
  consensus test passes unit values to the method instead of markers.
- The permutation null runs the same method on permuted phenotypes, with the
  permuted p-values in a matrix of markers by permutations.
- `ld_outlier_scan()` and `ld_region_rotation()` take these results in the same
  way as in `vignette("LDscnR_stage1_outlier_regions")`.
